## AEW All Out (2021) — overview

**All Out (2021)** was an **All Elite Wrestling** pay-per-view event held on **September 5, 2021**, at the **NOW Arena** in **Hoffman Estates, Illinois**, near Chicago. It is widely regarded as one of AEW’s most important and best-received shows, largely because of its major matches, the Chicago crowd, and the surprise debuts/returns at the end of the night.

It was the **third All Out** event in AEW history, following the 2019 and 2020 editions.

---

# Key significance

All Out 2021 is remembered for several major reasons:

- **CM Punk’s first wrestling match in over seven years**
- **The Lucha Brothers winning the AEW World Tag Team Championship** in a highly acclaimed steel cage match against The Young Bucks
- **Ruby Soho’s AEW debut**
- **Adam Cole’s AEW debut**
- **Bryan Danielson’s AEW debut**
- **Minoru Suzuki appearing after Jon Moxley’s match**
- One of AEW’s strongest critical and fan receptions to that point

The event helped cement AEW as a serious major-league alternative in North American wrestling and was seen by many as a major momentum-shifting moment for the company.

---

# Venue and broadcast details

- **Promotion:** All Elite Wrestling  
- **Event:** All Out 2021  
- **Date:** September 5, 2021  
- **Venue:** NOW Arena  
- **Location:** Hoffman Estates, Illinois, United States  
- **Attendance:** Around 10,000+ fans  
- **Broadcast:** Pay-per-view, B/R Live in the U.S., FITE internationally  
- **Commentary:** Jim Ross, Tony Schiavone, Excalibur, with others appearing during the show

---

# Full results

## The Buy-In pre-show

### Best Friends, Jurassic Express & Orange Cassidy defeated The Hardy Family Office

**Match:**  
Orange Cassidy, Chuck Taylor, Wheeler Yuta, Jungle Boy & Luchasaurus  
vs.  
Matt Hardy, Private Party, The Butcher & The Blade

**Result:** Best Friends/Jurassic Express/Orange Cassidy won.

This was a ten-man tag match used to energize the crowd before the main card. It featured a lot of the comedic and chaotic multi-man action associated with Orange Cassidy and the Best Friends, plus the athleticism of Jurassic Express.

---

# Main card

## 1. Miro defeated Eddie Kingston  
### AEW TNT Championship

**Champion:** Miro  
**Challenger:** Eddie Kingston  
**Result:** Miro retained the TNT Championship.

This opened the pay-per-view proper. Miro was in the middle of his “Redeemer” TNT title reign, portraying himself as a brutal, almost religious destroyer. Eddie Kingston was the gritty, street-fighting underdog.

The match was physical and hard-hitting. Kingston came close to winning, but Miro retained after some controversy involving the turnbuckle and a low blow before finishing Kingston.

---

## 2. Jon Moxley defeated Satoshi Kojima

**Result:** Jon Moxley won.

Jon Moxley faced Japanese legend **Satoshi Kojima** in a match that reflected AEW’s growing relationship with Japanese wrestling and Moxley’s own interest in strong-style and deathmatch-influenced opponents.

After the match, **Minoru Suzuki** made a surprise appearance and attacked Moxley. This set up the “Suzuki Incident” storyline and a later match between Moxley and Suzuki on AEW Dynamite.

The Chicago crowd reacted strongly to Suzuki’s arrival, as he was a major cult favorite among hardcore wrestling fans.

---

## 3. Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. defeated Kris Statlander  
### AEW Women’s World Championship

**Champion:** Britt Baker  
**Challenger:** Kris Statlander  
**Result:** Britt Baker retained.

Britt Baker was in the early stages of her first AEW Women’s World Championship reign. Kris Statlander challenged as a popular babyface associated with Best Friends and Orange Cassidy.

Baker retained after using her signature submission, the **Lockjaw**. The match helped continue Baker’s run as the central figure of AEW’s women’s division at the time.

---

## 4. The Lucha Brothers defeated The Young Bucks  
### Steel Cage match for the AEW World Tag Team Championship

**Champions:** The Young Bucks  
**Challengers:** Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix  
**Result:** The Lucha Brothers won the AEW World Tag Team Championship.

This is often considered the best match of the night and one of the best tag team matches in AEW history.

The match took place inside a steel cage and featured:

- High-risk offense from Rey Fénix
- Brutal superkicks and tandem attacks from The Young Bucks
- Dramatic near-falls
- Heavy crowd investment
- Penta’s family being shown at ringside
- The emotional moment of the Lucha Brothers finally winning the AEW tag titles

The Young Bucks entered as champions during their heel run as part of The Elite. The Lucha Brothers’ victory was one of the most emotional title changes AEW had produced up to that point.

Rey Fénix’s aerial work, including dives from the cage, became one of the defining images of the event.

---

## 5. Women’s Casino Battle Royale  
### Winner received a future AEW Women’s World Championship match

**Winner:** Ruby Soho

The Casino Battle Royale used AEW’s playing-card format, with groups of wrestlers entering based on suits and a final “Joker” entrant.

The surprise Joker entrant was **Ruby Soho**, formerly known as Ruby Riott in WWE. Her debut received a strong reaction.

Ruby Soho won the match by last eliminating **Thunder Rosa**, earning a future AEW Women’s World Championship match against Britt Baker.

This was Ruby’s first major AEW appearance and immediately positioned her as a significant player in the women’s division.

---

## 6. Chris Jericho defeated MJF  
### “Final Fight” stipulation

**Stipulation:** If Chris Jericho lost, he could never wrestle in AEW again.  
**Result:** Chris Jericho defeated MJF.

This was the climax of Jericho’s feud with **MJF** and the larger Inner Circle vs. Pinnacle rivalry.

MJF had already defeated Jericho multiple times in the lead-up to this match, including during the “Five Labours of Jericho” storyline. At All Out, Jericho put his AEW in-ring career on the line.

There was a false finish where MJF appeared to win after the referee missed Jericho’s foot on the rope. The match was restarted, and Jericho eventually won by submission with the **Walls of Jericho**.

This preserved Jericho’s AEW wrestling career and gave him revenge over MJF.

---

## 7. CM Punk defeated Darby Allin  
### CM Punk’s return match

**Result:** CM Punk won.

This was CM Punk’s first professional wrestling match since January 2014.

Punk had made his AEW debut on the August 20, 2021 episode of **Rampage: The First Dance** at the United Center in Chicago. His first opponent was Darby Allin, who was accompanied by Sting.

The match was built around mutual respect. Darby represented AEW’s younger generation, while Punk was the returning legend testing whether he could still compete.

Punk won with the **Go To Sleep**.

The match was not an over-the-top spectacle; it was more of a measured, story-driven return match designed to show Punk shaking off ring rust while still being able to hang with AEW talent.

Afterward, Punk, Darby, and Sting showed respect to one another.

---

## 8. Paul Wight defeated QT Marshall

**Result:** Paul Wight won.

This was Paul Wight’s AEW in-ring debut after signing with the company. He had previously been known for decades in WWE as **The Big Show**.

He faced QT Marshall of The Factory in a short match. Wight won decisively with a chokeslam.

This was more of a cooldown/special attraction match than a major competitive bout.

---

## 9. Kenny Omega defeated Christian Cage  
### AEW World Championship

**Champion:** Kenny Omega  
**Challenger:** Christian Cage  
**Result:** Kenny Omega retained.

Kenny Omega entered as AEW World Champion and leader of The Elite. Christian Cage had recently defeated Omega on the first episode of **AEW Rampage** to win the Impact World Championship, which added intrigue to the All Out title match.

At All Out, Omega retained the AEW World Championship after a hard-fought main event.

After the match, The Elite attacked Christian Cage and Jurassic Express. This led to one of the most famous closing segments in AEW history.

---

# The ending: Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson debut

After Kenny Omega retained the AEW World Championship, The Elite celebrated and beat down Christian Cage and Jurassic Express.

Then the lights went out.

## Adam Cole debuts

**Adam Cole** appeared, making his AEW debut after leaving WWE/NXT. At first, it looked like he might confront Kenny Omega and The Elite.

Instead, Cole superkicked Jungle Boy and joined The Elite, reuniting with Omega and The Young Bucks. This made sense historically because Cole, Omega, and the Bucks had all been connected through Bullet Club and The Elite lore before AEW existed.

Cole’s debut was a major moment, but AEW was not finished.

## Bryan Danielson debuts

Moments later, **Bryan Danielson**, formerly Daniel Bryan in WWE, debuted to a massive reaction.

Danielson came out to confront The Elite and helped even the odds alongside Christian Cage, Jurassic Express, and others.

The show ended with Danielson standing tall, signaling that AEW had added one of the most acclaimed wrestlers of his generation.

The back-to-back debuts of Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson are considered one of the most memorable endings to any AEW pay-per-view.

---

# Championships involved

Three AEW championships were defended on the main card:

## AEW TNT Championship
- **Miro defeated Eddie Kingston**
- Miro retained

## AEW Women’s World Championship
- **Britt Baker defeated Kris Statlander**
- Baker retained

## AEW World Tag Team Championship
- **The Lucha Brothers defeated The Young Bucks**
- New champions crowned

## AEW World Championship
- **Kenny Omega defeated Christian Cage**
- Omega retained

The only title change of the night was the **AEW World Tag Team Championship**, won by the Lucha Brothers.

---

# Notable debuts and appearances

## CM Punk
Not a debut, technically, because he had already debuted on AEW Rampage, but All Out 2021 was his first AEW match and first wrestling match in more than seven years.

## Ruby Soho
Debuted as the Joker in the Women’s Casino Battle Royale and won.

## Minoru Suzuki
Appeared after Jon Moxley’s match and attacked him.

## Adam Cole
Made his AEW debut after the main event and joined The Elite.

## Bryan Danielson
Made his AEW debut at the very end of the show and confronted The Elite.

---

# Match card summary

| Match | Result |
|---|---|
| Best Friends/Jurassic Express/Orange Cassidy vs. Hardy Family Office | Best Friends/Jurassic Express/Orange Cassidy won |
| Miro vs. Eddie Kingston — TNT Championship | Miro retained |
| Jon Moxley vs. Satoshi Kojima | Moxley won |
| Britt Baker vs. Kris Statlander — Women’s World Championship | Baker retained |
| Young Bucks vs. Lucha Brothers — Steel Cage Tag Title match | Lucha Brothers won the titles |
| Women’s Casino Battle Royale | Ruby Soho won |
| Chris Jericho vs. MJF | Jericho won |
| CM Punk vs. Darby Allin | CM Punk won |
| Paul Wight vs. QT Marshall | Paul Wight won |
| Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage — AEW World Championship | Omega retained |

---

# Critical reception

All Out 2021 received extremely positive reviews from fans and critics.

The most praised match was almost universally:

## The Young Bucks vs. The Lucha Brothers

The steel cage tag title match was praised for its athleticism, drama, pacing, and emotional payoff. Many fans considered it one of the best tag team matches of the modern era.

Other widely praised elements included:

- CM Punk’s return match atmosphere
- The surprise debuts
- Miro vs. Eddie Kingston as a strong opener
- The overall pacing and crowd energy
- The feeling that AEW was entering a new era

Some criticism was directed at:

- Paul Wight vs. QT Marshall feeling unnecessary or like a cooldown
- Minor production/timing issues
- The main event being somewhat overshadowed by the post-match debuts

But overall, the event was viewed as a major success.

---

# Legacy

All Out 2021 is often seen as one of AEW’s defining pay-per-views.

Its legacy includes:

- Elevating AEW’s perception as a true destination for major wrestling stars
- Giving CM Punk a successful in-ring return
- Creating one of AEW’s most beloved title-change moments with the Lucha Brothers
- Introducing Adam Cole and Bryan Danielson to AEW
- Strengthening AEW’s momentum during one of the hottest periods in company history

For many fans, the closing sequence of **Adam Cole joining The Elite** followed by **Bryan Danielson debuting** is one of the most iconic endings in AEW history.
